diagnostics.message: aws_lambda_function.pool is created with a dynamic vpc_config, so its execution role must hold the VPC-access policy at function-creation time. The function currently depends only on aws_iam_role.pool, not on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role, so the policy attachment can be applied after the function and Lambda creation fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2". Add an explicit depends_on to the attachment (no attribute reference can express this).

aws_lambda_function.pool relies on aws_iam_role_policy.pool for its runtime permissions (SSM parameter access, EC2 describe/launch, etc.). Nothing orders the attachment of this policy before the function is invoked (the scheduler can invoke it as soon as the apply completes), so an early invocation can fail with AccessDenied. Add a depends_on from the function to aws_iam_role_policy.pool.

When tracing is enabled (var.tracing_config.mode != null), the function's tracing_config makes it emit X-Ray segments, which requires aws_iam_role_policy.pool_xray to be attached. The function does not depend on that policy, so X-Ray calls can be denied if the function is invoked before the policy is attached. Add a depends_on from the function to aws_iam_role_policy.pool_xray (conditional on tracing).

When var.config.ami_id_ssm_parameter_name is set, the function reads the AMI SSM parameter at runtime and needs aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read attached. The function does not depend on this attachment, so the read can fail with AccessDenied if invoked before the policy is attached. Add a depends_on from the function to aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read.

aws_scheduler_schedule.pool uses aws_iam_role.scheduler to invoke the Lambda, but the role's invoke permission is granted by aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, which the schedule does not depend on. Early scheduled invocations (e.g. a near-immediate rate expression) can fail to invoke the function until that policy is attached. Add a depends_on from the schedule to aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler.
